title: observability: add token-level kv-cache hit/miss metrics and dashboards, tune alerts
author: Priya Menon
description: Add token-level KV cache metrics (kv_cache_hits_total, kv_cache_misses_total, kv_cache_hit_rate, kv_cache_lookup_duration_seconds histogram) with model_id and route labels, surface aggregated and per-model panels in Grafana, and introduce tuned alerting rules and a runbook. Motivation: teams observed intermittent latency/cost regressions caused by KV cache misses after model rollouts and cache expiry; having token-level visibility lets SRE and runtime engineers correlate miss spikes with regressed tail latency and token cost. Changes: instrument runtime KV cache to emit Prometheus metrics and OpenTelemetry spans for cache lookups, add Prometheus alert rules for sustained low hit-rate and elevated lookup latency, create a Grafana dashboard with token-level breakdowns and heatmap of hit-rate by route/model, add runbook with troubleshooting steps and automated remediation suggestions, and include unit/integration tests and example quickstart. Checklist: [x] runtime instrumentation added, [x] Prometheus rules and alerts, [x] Grafana dashboard and panels, [x] runbook and docs, [x] tests, [x] CI green. Related: ENG-10234 implements the new token-level cost accounting hooks used by these metrics. This PR is intended to be backward-compatible but increases metric cardinality by adding model_id and route labels; labels are scoped and scrubbed to limit cardinality per SRE guidelines.

feat(observability): add Prometheus alert rules for kv cache hit-rate and lookup latency

review_conversation: Evelyn Park: Please ensure we keep metric cardinality low; model_id is required but route should be optional. Can we sanitize route values to canonical names?
Priya Menon: Good catch. I added a sanitizer to map routes to canonical IDs and added a config flag to disable route label per-service when cardinality is a concern.

Carlos Mendes: Alert thresholds look aggressive for high-QPS models. Recommend changing sustained window to 10m and adding a burn rate style alert for rapid drops. Also add a note in the runbook about rolling back recent model variants.

Priya Menon: Tuned thresholds per suggestion: sustained 10m window for low hit rate and a short-window burn alert for >=20% drop over 3m. Runbook updated with rollback steps and suggested canary checks.
Jordan Li: Add histogram buckets for lookup latency to capture sub-ms tail; also include exemplar spans for span linking in traces.
Priya Menon: Added buckets [0.1ms,0.5ms,1ms,2ms,5ms,10ms,50ms] and added OTEL exemplar sampling on misses. Added tests for exemplar emission.
Evelyn Park: CI flake on metrics test - looks like a race on the histogram; can you add deterministic seeding in test?
Priya Menon: Fixed with deterministic clock in tests and mocked prometheus registry. All tests reran and passed.
ci_details: integration-tests: pass after rerun (flaky histogram test fixed)
release_notes: Added token-level KV cache metrics (hits, misses, hit_rate, lookup_latency) with Grafana dashboard and tuned alerts + runbook. Operators can opt out of adding route labels to limit cardinality. Improves visibility into cache-related latency and cost regressions.
notes: Metric naming follows prometheus conventions and existing observability naming guidelines. Cardinality mitigation: route label sanitized and optional. Runbook includes automated remediation suggestions and links to rollback procedures. This PR required a minor infra change to load additional alert rules via terraform; ops notified.
testing_summary: Added unit tests for metric counters and histograms, integration test that simulates cache hit/miss patterns and asserts alert firing behavior under TTL expiry conditions, deterministic replay used to avoid test flakiness.
